wins.text: NIKE Running grew high single digits overall in Q4, with Vomero 18 becoming a $100M+ franchise in just over 90 days with strong sell-through across all geographies
Holiday order book is up year-over-year with growth in North America, EMEA, and APLA, signaling improving wholesale partner confidence
Women's basketball business expanded more than 50% for the full fiscal year; A'ja Wilson's A'One signature shoe sold out in 3 minutes on NIKE Digital in North America
EMEA Sportswear grew overall in wholesale in Q4 and women's sportswear footwear returned to growth; NIKE Digital delivered double-digit increase in share of demand at full price

New Amazon partnership announced for fall, featuring a dedicated brand store across running, training, basketball and sportswear; also expanded distribution with Urban Outfitters, Aritzia (200+ women's-led doors), and running specialty accounts

risks.text: Q4 revenues declined 12% reported / 11% currency-neutral; gross margins fell 440 bps to 40.3% driven by higher wholesale discounts, factory store discounts, supply chain cost deleverage and channel mix headwinds
Classic footwear franchises (Air Force 1, Dunk, AJ1) declined more than 30% in Q4, representing nearly a $1 billion revenue headwind; declines expected to continue through first half of FY'26

Tariffs represent an estimated gross incremental cost increase of approximately $1 billion; expected net impact of ~75 bps to gross margin in FY'26 with greater impact in H1; Q1 alone absorbs ~100 bps tariff headwind

Greater China Q4 revenue declined 20%, EBIT declined 45%; traffic remains challenged, digital remains highly promotional, and full recovery expected to take significantly longer than other geographies
NIKE Digital traffic expected to be down double digits throughout all of FY'26 as company repositions the channel to a full-price model; Digital declined 26% in Q4 globally

guidance_items.detail: Q1 FY'26 revenues expected to be down mid-single digits; Digital traffic expected down double digits for full FY'26; second half faces modest revenue headwind lapping prior-year aggressive clearance activity

Q1 gross margins expected down approximately 350-425 bps including ~100 bps tariff impact; full-year tariff net impact ~75 bps to gross margin; margins remain under pressure in H1 before moderating in H2
SG&A expected to grow low single digits in FY'26; other income/expense including net interest income guided to $0-$10M in Q1; full-year tax rate guided to 19%-20%
Holiday order book up YoY with growth in North America, EMEA, and APLA; wholesale momentum building as channel cleans up and product portfolio transitions
Share repurchases moderated in near term due to dynamic environment and Win Now financial impacts; strong balance sheet maintained as competitive advantage

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Structural long-term operating margin potential once Win Now actions clear — whether double-digit margins are still achievable
Specific cadence and timeline for China recovery including competitive dynamics and monobrand marketplace challenges
Trade-off between gross margin recovery and unit volume/revenue as company laps aggressive clearance activity in H2 FY'26
